items.title: Section: The Seventh Angle Opens — Distinguishing the First Five Powers, Each From the Power Right Beside It

items.zh: 謂此十力展轉相望，亦有差別，亦無差別。處非處智力等與自業智力等，有何差別？若正了知善不善業，能感所有愛非愛果，當知此由處非處智力故。若正了知諸有能造善不善業，即彼能受愛非愛果，而非所餘，當知此由自業智力故。若正了知諸有能修靜慮、解脫、等持、等至，即彼能入靜慮等定，而非所餘，當知此由自業智力故。若正了知即依如是靜慮等定，現三神變，無倒教授所化有情，當知此由靜慮、解脫、等持、等至智力故。若正照取信等俱生相應之心，當知此由靜慮、解脫、等持、等至智力故。若正分別即彼諸根軟中上品種種差別，當知此由根勝劣智力故。若正照取諸根為先，彼彼法中種種意樂，當知此由根勝劣智力故。若正分別即彼意樂種種差別，當知此由種種勝解智力故。
items.en:
Second, stating. These ten powers, considered in relation to one another, are both distinct and not distinct.
Third, explaining; first, the general question of distinction. What distinguishes the power regarding what is possible and impossible, and so forth, from the power regarding karma, and so forth?
Second, distinguishing each in turn; first, the first and second powers; first, the power regarding what is possible and impossible. Truly knowing that wholesome and unwholesome karma can bring about desirable and undesirable results — know this belongs to the power regarding what is possible and impossible.
Second, the power regarding karma. Truly knowing that whoever performs wholesome or unwholesome karma is precisely the one who experiences the desirable or undesirable result, and no other — know this belongs to the power regarding karma.
Second, the second and third powers; first, the power regarding karma. Truly knowing that whoever can cultivate meditative absorption, liberation, equipoise, and attainment is precisely the one who enters such absorption, and no other — know this belongs to the power regarding karma.
Second, the power regarding meditative absorptions. Truly knowing that, relying on such absorption, three kinds of miraculous transformation can be manifested to teach beings without distortion — know this belongs to the power regarding meditative absorptions.
Third, the third and fourth powers; first, the power regarding meditative absorptions. Truly perceiving the mind arising together with, and associated with, faith and the rest — know this belongs to the power regarding meditative absorptions.
Second, the power regarding superior and inferior faculties. Truly distinguishing the various inferior, middling, and superior grades of those same faculties — know this belongs to the power regarding superior and inferior faculties.
Fourth, the fourth and fifth powers; first, the power regarding faculties. Truly perceiving, on the basis of such faculties, the various resolute inclinations within each specific phenomenon — know this belongs to the power regarding faculties.
Second, the power regarding various resolute inclinations; first, stating its characteristic. Truly distinguishing the various differences among those same inclinations — know this belongs to the power regarding various resolute inclinations.

items.title: Section: Six Kinds of Resolute Inclination — From Longing for Godhood to Vowing Never to Rush Into Nirvāṇa

items.zh: 即彼意樂，當知分別略有六種。一者、不出離意樂。謂於各別大自在天、那羅延天、梵世間等起信解者所有意樂。二者、出離意樂。謂於三乘起信解者所有意樂。三者、遠清淨意樂。謂安住下品、中品成熟者所有意樂。四者、近清淨意樂。謂安住上品成熟者所有意樂。五者、即於現法得涅槃意樂。謂由聲聞乘所得涅槃起信解者所有意樂。六者、於當來世得涅槃意樂。謂由大乘所得涅槃起信解者所有意樂。
items.en:
Second, explaining the distinctions; first, presenting the six inclinations. These inclinations, know, are in brief of six kinds.
Second, listing and explaining each; first, the inclination not to leave. First, the inclination not to leave: the inclination of those placing faith and confidence in various individual heavenly lords — the Great Sovereign Deity, Nārāyaṇa, the Brahmā heavens.
Second, the inclination to leave. Second, the inclination to leave: the inclination of those placing faith and confidence in the three vehicles.
Third, the inclination far from purity. Third, the inclination far from purity: the inclination of those abiding at an inferior or middling stage of maturation.
Fourth, the inclination near purity. Fourth, the inclination near purity: the inclination of those abiding at the superior stage of maturation.
Fifth, the inclination to attain nirvāṇa in this very life. Fifth, the inclination to attain nirvāṇa in this very life: the inclination of those placing faith and confidence in the nirvāṇa attained through the śrāvaka vehicle.
Sixth, the inclination to attain nirvāṇa in a future life. Sixth, the inclination to attain nirvāṇa in a future life: the inclination of those placing faith and confidence in the nirvāṇa attained through the Great Vehicle.

items.title: Section: The Final Five Pairwise Distinctions, and the Four Kinds of Seed Underlying the Sixth Power

items.zh: 若正照取勝解所起相似種子，當知此由種種勝解智力故。若正照取即彼種子差別分別無量品類，當知此由種種界智力故。又即彼界，當知分別略有四種。一者、本性住種子。二者、先習起種子。三者、可修治種子，謂有般涅槃法者所有種子。四者、不可修治種子，謂無般涅槃法者所有種子。若正了知如界種類行跡趣入，當知此由種種界智力故。若正分別即彼行跡一切品類，如是行跡能令離染，如是行跡能令畢竟清淨，如是行跡能令不畢竟清淨，當知此由遍趣行智力故。若如實知前際隨念一切趣因前際俱行，當知此由遍趣行智力故。若正了知如前分別種種隨順八言說句、六種略行，當知此由宿住隨念智力故。若正了知依於前際有情死生，當知此由宿住隨念智力故。若正觀見後際種種有情死生，當知此由死生智力故。若正了知於自事義未得究竟，有情後際受生相續，當知此由死生智力故。若正了知於自事義已得究竟，心善解脫，於現法中證得涅槃，當知此由漏盡智力故。當知是名如來十力展轉相望，亦有差別，亦無差別。
items.en:
Fifth, the fifth and sixth powers; first, the power regarding resolute inclinations. Truly perceiving the seeds resembling what arises from resolute understanding — know this belongs to the power regarding resolute inclinations.
Second, the power regarding elements; first, stating its characteristic. Truly perceiving the immeasurable distinct categories into which those same seeds further divide — know this belongs to the power regarding elements.
Second, explaining the distinction; first, presenting the kinds. These same elements, know, are in brief of four kinds.
Second, listing and explaining. First, seeds abiding by nature. Second, seeds arisen through prior habituation. Third, seeds capable of cultivation — belonging to those possessing the capacity for complete nirvāṇa. Fourth, seeds incapable of cultivation — belonging to those lacking the capacity for complete nirvāṇa.
Sixth, the sixth and seventh powers; first, the power regarding elements. Truly knowing the kind of element underlying one's path and gateway of entry — know this belongs to the power regarding elements.
Second, the power regarding paths to every destination. Truly distinguishing every category of that same path — which lead to freedom from defilement, which lead to complete purity, which lead only to incomplete purity — know this belongs to the power regarding paths to every destination.
Seventh, the seventh and eighth powers; first, the power regarding paths to every destination. Truly knowing, through recollecting the past, the karmic cause behind every destiny together with its accompanying factors — know this belongs to the power regarding paths to every destination.
Second, the power recollecting past abodes. Truly knowing, as previously distinguished, the eight sayings and six abbreviated conducts — know this belongs to the power recollecting past abodes.
Eighth, the eighth and ninth powers; first, the power recollecting past abodes. Truly knowing a being's death and rebirth with respect to the past — know this belongs to the power recollecting past abodes.
Second, the power regarding death and rebirth. Truly observing a being's death and rebirth with respect to the future — know this belongs to the power regarding death and rebirth.
Ninth, the ninth and tenth powers; first, the power regarding death and rebirth. Truly knowing that a being's own task remains incomplete, destined to continue being reborn — know this belongs to the power regarding death and rebirth.
Second, the power regarding the exhaustion of outflows. Truly knowing that a being's own task has reached completion, the mind fully liberated, nirvāṇa realised in this very life — know this belongs to the power regarding the exhaustion of outflows.
Fourth, concluding. Know this is called how the Tathāgata's ten powers, considered in relation to one another, are both distinct and not distinct.

items.title: Section: The Four Fearlessnesses Named — Continuing Directly Where Fascicle 49 Left Off

items.zh: 如來所有四無畏文，如契經說應知其相。
items.en: Fourth, the four fearlessnesses; first, pointing to what the sūtras say. The Tathāgata's own text on the four fearlessnesses should be understood in its characteristics exactly as the sūtras teach.

items.title: Section: Four Grounds for Self-Praise, and Why Ordinary Disciples Should Never Attempt the Same

items.zh: 謂諸如來，於其四處，在大眾中而自稱歎。謂所知障永解脫故，於一切種一切法中現等正覺，不共聲聞，是第一處。諸煩惱障永解脫故，證得漏盡共諸聲聞，是第二處。為求解脫諸有情類超過眾苦說出離道，是第三處。即於能出道得為礙，說諸障法應當遠離，是第四處。如來既於如是四處，如其實義自稱歎已。次後他於自所稱歎前之二處，所有相違身語意業而興謗難；
items.en:
Second, briefly explaining the meaning; first, presenting the four grounds; first, stating. The Tathāgatas, regarding these four grounds, praise themselves before the great assembly.
Second, listing them; first, directly awakening. Because he has permanently liberated himself from the obstruction of the knowable, he directly and equally awakens to every phenomenon of every kind, not shared with śrāvakas; this is the first ground.
Second, attaining exhausted outflows. Because he has permanently liberated himself from the obstruction of affliction, he attains the exhaustion of outflows, shared with śrāvakas; this is the second ground.
Third, teaching the path of transcendence. For the sake of beings seeking liberation to transcend every suffering, he teaches the path of transcendence; this is the third ground.
Fourth, teaching the obstructing phenomena. Regarding what obstructs the very path of transcendence, he teaches the obstructing phenomena that should be abandoned; this is the fourth ground.
Second, explaining why called fearless. The Tathāgata, having thus truthfully praised himself regarding these four grounds, subsequently faces objections from others claiming that his own visible conduct of body, speech, and mind contradicts the first two of these self-praised grounds.

blocks.text: How each power differs from its neighbour, and then the four fearlessnesses: the Buddha's four confident claims, which no one can rightly challenge.

Venerable Miào Jìng: 俱生 here means "arising at the same time". The first power knows that deeds bring results; the second, that only the doer receives them. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first stresses the principle of cause and effect itself.

The first: those who trust in heavenly lords. Venerable Miào Jìng: believing in Brahmā feels lofty, yet cannot leave the sea of suffering. On the higher grades: from the stage of patience up is "superior". Master Cháng Bǎi: heat and peak can still regress.
Venerable Miào Jìng: not from habituation or practice alone; without the seed, habituation cannot make it arise.

Freed from the obstruction of the knowable, he awakens to all phenomena. Venerable Miào Jìng: what obstructs knowing is the obstruction of the knowable. 正覺 awakens to the ultimate, 等覺 to the conventional. The second fearlessness, freedom from contaminants, is shared with śrāvakas: Master Cháng Bǎi, the three vehicles sit on the same bed of liberation.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha sometimes asks questions he knows the answer to. Master Cháng Bǎi: a deliberate display, not ignorance. And with Devadatta: Venerable Miào Jìng, he needed such words to be subdued; Master Cháng Bǎi, the Buddha was compassionate towards him, never angry.
"The three vehicles sit on the same bed of liberation." Master Cháng Bǎi's image is a reminder that the arhat's freedom is real freedom.

quiz.q: "Mind arising together with faculties such as faith" is rendered "innate." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read 俱生?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 俱生 means arising at the same time. The English "innate" does not fit here.

quiz.q: How are the first two powers distinguished?
options: the first knows deeds bring results; the second that the doer is the one who receives
quiz.why: The first knows that deeds bring results; the second that the doer alone receives them. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first stresses the principle of cause and effect itself.

quiz.q: Whose is the inclination not to leave?
options: those trusting the Great Sovereign Deity, Nārāyaṇa, the Brahmā heavens
quiz.why: Those trusting heavenly lords. Venerable Miào Jìng: believing in Brahmā feels lofty, yet cannot leave the sea of suffering.

quiz.q: To what stages do the lectures assign "far from" and "near" purity?
options: near = patience and above; far = heat and peak, where roots can still regress
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: from patience up is the superior grade. Master Cháng Bǎi: patience and the world's foremost are near the path of seeing; heat and peak can still regress.

quiz.q: How do seeds abiding by nature relate to seeds arisen through habituation?
options: the first isn't from habituation; without it, habituation cannot arise
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: not from habituation or practice; without the seed, habituation cannot make it arise. Master Cháng Bǎi says the same of the store consciousness.

quiz.q: What is the first ground, and why is it not shared with śrāvakas?
options: freed from the obstruction of the knowable, directly awakening to every phenomenon
quiz.why: Freed from the obstruction of the knowable, he awakens to all phenomena — not shared with śrāvakas. Venerable Miào Jìng: what obstructs knowing is the obstruction of the knowable.

quiz.q: How do the lectures distinguish 等覺 and 正覺 in "directly awakening"?
options: agreed: 正覺 fundamental, 等覺 subsequent wisdom; Miào Jìng: ultimate and conventional truths
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 正覺 awakens to the ultimate, 等覺 to the conventional. Master Cháng Bǎi: 等覺 is subsequent, 正覺 fundamental wisdom. "Directly and equally" stays literal.

quiz.q: How does the second ground relate to śrāvakas?
quiz.why: Shared with śrāvakas. Master Cháng Bǎi: the three vehicles sit on the same bed of liberation, though the Buddha also has no residual habits.

quiz.q: Some charge that the Buddha asks questions, so he isn't omniscient. How do the lectures answer?
options: he asks knowingly, as a deliberate display
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha asks knowingly. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is a deliberate display, not ignorance.

quiz.q: The Buddha rebuked Devadatta yet spoke gently to Rāhula. How do the lectures answer the charge of anger and love?
options: both: speech fits the person; Miào Jìng: Devadatta was evil and needed such words; Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha was always compassionate to him
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: Devadatta needed such words to be subdued. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha was compassionate towards Devadatta, never angry.
